cards.text: Amos, one of the sheepherders of Tekoa, carries the LORD's word concerning Israel (Amos 1:1). He's just delivered the LORD's judgment on Israel for selling the needy for a pair of sandals (Amos 2:6). Now he says, "Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, O children of Israel," and the LORD has more to say.

cards.question: The LORD's word is against the whole family He brought up out of the land of ___.
Out of all the families of the earth, the LORD says He has known only Israel. So what does He say He will do because of that?

answers.text: Punish them for all their iniquities

cards.text: Hold on. "Only you have I known," and then "therefore I will punish you"? That's the boss saying "You're my favorite" and in the SAME breath, "Come to my office."
Then the questions start coming, one after another, like a drumbeat. "Can two walk together without agreeing where to go?"

cards.question: Next the questions turn to a lion in the forest. What do they point to about when a lion roars?

answers.text: He roars when he has prey
He roars when a storm comes
He roars to call his pride

cards.question: Then come a bird and a snare. The question about them points to bait having been set.
And when a trap springs from the ground, what do the questions say it must have?

cards.text: Now the picture leaves the forest and walks right into a city. A ram's horn sounds.

cards.question: When a ram's horn sounds in a city, what do the questions say the people do?
The questions then turn to calamity coming to a city. They point to the LORD as the One who caused it.

cards.text: Every one of these questions works the same way: something happens, and there's a reason it happened. When the smoke alarm goes off in my bakery, I don't stand there asking WHY, friend, I KNOW I burnt the batch.

cards.question: Surely the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing His plan first. Who does He reveal it to?

cards.text: Then comes the line this whole passage is named after. "The lion has roared—who will not fear?"

cards.question: In the second half of that line, the Lord GOD has spoken. What does the prophet say no one could keep from doing?

cards.text: The Lord GOD speaks, so the prophet speaks. When an angel showed up at my junk drawer, I asked for ONE minute, and I spent it writing a goodbye note, not a list of excuses.
Now a call goes out to the citadels of Ashdod, a Philistine city (Amos 1:8), and to the citadels of Egypt. They're told to assemble on the mountains of Samaria and take a good look.

cards.question: Ashdod and Egypt are invited to the mountains of Samaria. What are they told to see in the city?

answers.text: The great unrest and acts of oppression
The new walls going up around it
The great feast being held there

cards.question: The LORD says the people of that city know how to do right.

cards.text: A citadel is where you keep the good stuff, and mine would be FULL of chocolate chips. The LORD says theirs are stocked with something else.

cards.question: The LORD says they store up ___ and ___ in their citadels.
Therefore the Lord GOD says what's coming for the land. What is it?

answers.text: A drought will dry it out

cards.text: That enemy will pull down their strongholds and plunder their citadels. All that violence stored up in there, and now somebody's coming to clean the place out.
Then the LORD gives a picture I bet Amos the sheepherder knew well: a shepherd snatching from the mouth of the lion two legs or a piece of an ear.

cards.question: Like that shepherd's rescue, the Israelites dwelling in Samaria will come out with almost nothing.

cards.text: Rescued, having just the corner of a bed or the cushion of a couch. That's calling the movers, and the only thing that makes it to the new place is ONE couch cushion.

cards.question: Next, the Lord GOD, the God of Hosts, calls out to hear and testify. Who is the testimony against?

cards.text: Then the LORD talks about the day He punishes Israel for their transgressions. He'll visit destruction on the altars of Bethel, the town where Jeroboam, king of Israel, once set up a golden calf (1 Kings 12:29).

cards.question: What does the LORD say will happen to the horns of the altar at Bethel?

answers.text: They'll be cut off and fall to the ground
They'll be covered in fresh gold again
They'll be carried off to the land of Egypt

cards.question: Then come the houses. The LORD says He'll tear down the winter house but leave the summer house standing.

cards.text: Winter house, summer house, houses of ivory, great houses, the LORD says they all come down. These folks had a house for every season, and I had ONE junk drawer that I shared with a rubber band.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 4 quotes "Come to my office.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card cites Amos 1:1 for 'carries the LORD's word concerning Israel.' Amos 1:1 calls them 'the words of Amos' and 'what he saw regarding Israel.' It does not call them the LORD's word.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 1 by a wide margin. Of its 9 choice cards, 6 are multiple choice, 2 are true or false and 1 is fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. It tells nothing new from the passage. Verses 3:4-6 were already told and asked on cards 6 to 11, and this card only sums up how those questions work, plus a joke.
The card says 'Every one of these questions,' which includes the question in 3:3 (card 5). But it cites only Amos 3:4-6.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. It only restates 3:8, which card 14 already told and card 15 already asked ('The Lord GOD speaks, so the prophet speaks'). It doesn't move the passage forward.

The joke's action doesn't match the verse. Amos 3:8 is about not being able to keep from speaking once God has spoken. The comparison is about spending a minute on a goodbye note instead of excuses, which is a different action. It also sits awkwardly with the backstory, where he did object first ('Look at me... My edges are gone'). The line doesn't click instantly.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The setup rules out the wrong answers on card 5. The card says a citadel is where you keep 'the good stuff,' and theirs are 'stocked with something else.' That eliminates silver, gold and grain, which are all good stuff, and leaves violence and destruction as the only possible picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: No earlier card says that the house of Jacob means Israel. A baker who doesn't already know Jacob was renamed Israel has no way to reason past the house of Esau or the house of Pharaoh. The story card before it (card 10) gives no context.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The card calls the king behind the Bethel golden calf (1 Kings 12:29) 'Jeroboam, king of Israel.' Amos 1:1 names a different Jeroboam, son of Jehoash, as king of Israel in Amos's own day. A baker could think they are the same king.
findings.question: When a name in an outside reference could be confused with a different person of the same name tied to the passage, should Papa Dorin tell them apart (for example, 'Jeroboam son of Nebat' or 'an earlier king'), or is 'once' enough?
